Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this RFI. We're working through vendor evidence for our upcoming audit and have a few focused questions about Redwood's audit ledger and exportability:

- Can you confirm whether the internal audit ledger is append-only and if you provide a tamper-evident checksum or signed manifest for export bundles?
- What are the minimum/maximum retention windows configurable for audit records (per-tenant and system-wide)? Any hard limits?
- For bulk exports, what query window granularity do you support (minute/hour/day), and are there APIs for sliced exports (timebox + user-id + request-id)?
- Do you support snapshotting a point-in-time ledger state and providing a signed attestation of integrity (e.g., hash tree root + timestamp)?

We're looking for short, concrete answers and examples of artifacts (manifest format, sample signed checksum, or playbook entries). If possible, please attach any existing playbooks or templates.

Hi Maria / Alcyon team,

Thanks — good, focused questions. Short answers up front, details below and attached: redwood_export_playbook_v1.pdf (playbook) and sampling_protocol_template.xlsx.

- Append-only & tamper evidence: Our audit ledger is write-once for finalized events. Exports include a manifest.json with per-file SHA-256 checksums and a signed bundle-level statement. For high-assurance customers we optionally provide a timestamped Merkle root signed by KMS-backed key (HSMinterop) — see page 6 of the playbook.

- Retention windows: Per-tenant retention is configurable from 30 days up to 10 years. System-wide hard limit enforced for hosted tenants is 10 years; on Private deployments customers can configure retention up to their legal limits. We also support tiered retention (hot/cold) and immutable forensic slices for legal hold.

- Query window granularity & slicing: Bulk export APIs support arbitrary time ranges with native slicing by ISO-8601 timestamps (min granularity 1 minute). Pre-built export helpers can slice by user_id, request_id, model_id, and route. You can request NDJSON or compressed Parquet outputs.

- Point-in-time snapshot & attestation: We support creating a snapshot (immutable export bundle) tied to a timestamp and a signed manifest. For Dedicated/Private customers we can provide a Merkle-root attestation (signed via customer-managed KMS if requested).

I've attached the playbook which includes manifest examples and a sample signed-attestation workflow under section 4.

Next steps: would you like a sample bundle (redacted) with a manifest and checksum we can deliver to your S3 bucket for testing? Also happy to schedule a short walkthrough with our evidence team.

Best,

Karthik Iyer

Maria — quick technical notes to supplement Karthik's answers: 

- Export manifest: our manifest layout is simple and compact. Example line: {"path":"audit/2026/08/09/part-0001.ndjson.gz", "sha256":"<hex>", "rows": 12453, "start_ts":"2026-08-09T00:00:00Z", "end_ts":"2026-08-09T23:59:59Z"}. We include a top-level bundle_manifest.json with a bundle_sha256 and created_at timestamp.

- Slicing APIs: /v1/admin/audit/exports supports POST {"query": {"from": "2026-08-01T00:00:00Z", "to": "2026-08-09T23:59:59Z"}, "slice_by": ["user_id", "request_id"], "format": "ndjson.gz"}. Responses return presigned S3 locations as they become available.

- Sampling protocol: our sampling template supports stratified random sampling by time window and user cohorts; we included a template (sampling_protocol_template.xlsx) for your audit team to specify strata and sample sizes.

If you want, we can run a 2-hour workshop to produce a sample export and provide the manifest + signed attestation into your acceptance S3.

Thanks,
Ben

Redwood Inference
